name: LDR-5
summary: A 20 m lander that sits down on four legs, carries six crew and two tonnes, and climbs back to orbit on the same tanks. Ugly on purpose: everything is outside the hull where it can be reached in a suit.

rooms.name: Flight Deck
rooms.description: Two seats under a wrapped forward window that looks down as well as ahead, because on the last thirty metres the crew are watching the ground, not the horizon. Landing is flown by the computer and supervised by hand; either seat can take over with a throttle and a stick. The window carries an etched horizon line for manual attitude if the displays go dark.

hotspots.title: Pilot Seat
hotspots.text: Both seats face 12° down so the crew see the pad on final.

hotspots.title: Throttle Quadrant
hotspots.text: Four levers, one per engine, ganged unless a crew splits them.

rooms.name: Cabin
rooms.description: Six jump seats along the walls with the floor clear between them, because everything the crew carry down rides on their backs or in the bay below. The cabin holds 101 kPa on the surface and drops to 55 kPa of oxygen-rich mix before an EVA, which cuts pre-breathe to twenty minutes. Two lights, one warm, one red for night landings.

hotspots.title: Jump Seat
hotspots.text: Folds flat against the wall. The floor is kept clear for suited crew.

hotspots.title: Cabin Light
hotspots.text: Warm for transit, red from ten minutes before a night landing.

rooms.name: Suit Station
rooms.description: Two suits on the aft bulkhead with their backs against the hull, so a crew member walks into one and seals it without help. Recharge is from the cabin loop: forty minutes for a full pack. The cabin itself is the airlock — the lander vents and repressurises rather than carrying a separate chamber, which costs 8 kg of gas a cycle and saves a tonne of structure.

rooms.name: Docking Collar
rooms.description: The dorsal port the lander hangs from while it is attached to a ship. It carries fuel, water and data as well as crew, so a lander can be refilled without anyone suiting up. The ring is the same androgynous pattern as the shuttle's, which means either craft can dock to either parent or to each other.

rooms.name: Cargo Bay & Ramp
rooms.description: An unpressurised bay slung under the deck with a ramp that reaches the ground at 24°. Two tonnes down, or one tonne up plus samples. The bay takes standard half-height cases on a 30 cm tie-down grid, and the ramp doubles as a work bench once the lander is on the surface and the engines have cooled.

hotspots.title: Ramp
hotspots.text: Lowers in 9 s. Rated to take the full payload in one pass.

rooms.name: Landing Gear
rooms.description: Four splayed legs with crushable cartridges in the struts, set wide enough to take a 12° slope and a 1.4 m boulder under one pad. The pads are 2.4 m discs that spread the load on dust. Each leg has a ring light so the crew can see what they are setting down on; the gear is the only part of the ship expected to be replaced after a hard landing.

rooms.name: Descent Engines
rooms.description: Four throttling engines at 26 kN each, deep enough to hover at 10% and strong enough to abort to orbit on three. They gimbal ±6°, which handles an engine out and a badly loaded bay at the same time. Everything the crew has to service is on the outside of the pods, reachable from the ramp with the gloves on.

hotspots.title: Engine Pod
hotspots.text: Serviced from the outside; the covers come off with gloves on.

systems.name: Power
systems.description: Two fuel cells under the cabin floor, with the engine pods drawing directly off the same bus.

systems.name: Atmos
systems.description: One loop for the two pressurised compartments. The cabin is also the airlock, so the loop has to refill it.

systems.name: Data
systems.description: Flight deck to everything. The gear and engine sensors are what the crew watch on the last thirty metres.

segments.name: Overview
segments.caption: Twenty metres of lander: a pressure can on four legs with everything serviceable on the outside.

segments.name: Cabin
segments.caption: Six jump seats and a clear floor, because everything else rides in the bay underneath.

segments.name: Flight Deck
segments.caption: Two seats and a wrapped window angled down, for the last thirty metres onto the pad.

segments.name: Docking Collar
segments.caption: The dorsal ring that takes crew, fuel, water and data from the parent ship.

segments.name: Cargo Ramp
segments.caption: Two tonnes down, one tonne back up, over a ramp that doubles as the surface work bench.

segments.name: Landing Gear
segments.caption: Four splayed legs with crushable struts, good for a twelve-degree slope and a boulder under one pad.

segments.name: Descent Engines
segments.caption: Four throttling engines: hover at a tenth of power, abort to orbit on any three.
